utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Court Deputy, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, before we hear the witness this afternoon, there's some housekeeping matters that we would like to deal with. Last Friday during the hearing, the OTP mentioned that they are awaiting decisions on the authentication binder and did not mention the other attached exhibits concerning with Stephanie Frease's testimony in the Krstic case. We have some questions to ask the Prosecution. The first one is that we looked into that materials, but we did not find any documents attached to Tab 6. I wonder whether the Prosecution would like to tender any documents under this tab, Tab 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, my recollection of Ms. Frease was the authentication binder was the main thing we were asking. As for the detail of precisely what we said was in Tab 6, and Ms. Stewart I can see is helping me out, and I know Ms. Davis was principally helping working on the exhibits related to the 92 bis witnesses. So I -- I don't have a precise answer for you, but I will very soon, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Another question is that we want to know whether you would like to tender other materials attached to Ms. Frease's Krstic testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The -- I know the theory of our 92 bis admissions and submissions was that in order to make full sense of the testimony, we wanted to attach the -- all the exhibits that the witness referred to, if it had not come in through another witness that had already come in as part of the 92 bis information. So that were -- those were our intentions. And I would have -- I believe we have tried to make that clear, but if we haven't, we will double check and find. There may be some extraneous things we just didn't think you needed to see or would be important to understand the testimony. But normally, if there's an exhibit that the witness refers to, it would just help have the testimony make sense, so that's why we would have offered exhibits like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I turn to Mr. Stojanovic. I think on the 23rd July, 2003, you requested that Ms. Frease would have to come for cross-examination, and I have not found any reference to this in the 18th December, 2003, transcript, which you claimed last Friday. Will you please clarify this issue for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour. On Wednesday, 23rd of July, we reiterated what we had submitted in writing in our motion regarding our objection to the admission of this testimony under Rules 92 bis and 94. So in light of our standing objection as to the credibility and quality of intercepts, and also bearing in mind the testimony of Ms. Stephanie Frease in the Krstic case, obviously there was need for our Defence to cross-examine her. And that was why we requested that. Now, what we wanted to achieve with this cross-examination of Ms. Stephanie Frease, first of all judging from the analysis that she had completed, we wanted to elicit the answers which indicate noncredibility of these intercepts. In particular, if we know that there is no single audio recording of the intercepts in which the name of Dragan Jokic would have been mentioned. So that was the basic reason why we requested the appearance of Ms. Stephanie Frease before this Tribunal, to state what her opinion is of these particular intercepts. Second, her testimony in the Krstic trial was focussed on the intercepts concerning the position of the Drina Corps and their quality, including, of course, the commander of the Drina Corps. In the current case, we have a different kind of intercepts concerning the 14th of July and a high-level intensity of the intercepts and a confusion that reigned in the air at the time, which we think is an important issue regarding the intercepts, and that is why we requested her testimony. And that is the reason why we wanted to have your decision on the issue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stojanovic. But I have to remind you that the Bench has already ruled upon the intercept matters by its intercept decision of the 18th December, 2003. I believe that the principles laid down in those intercepts are also applicable for any new intercepts in the so-called authentication binders. Well, Mr. McCloskey, I -- actually, I'm waiting for your clarification on this matter. If we got any clear answer on that issue, we believe we were in the position to make the decisions, no matter if it is oral or in written form. I hope you could inform us as soon as possible about your position on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I will double check on the exhibits that she had talked about in Krstic and the exhibits we have offered and make sure they are what we intended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I understand that before the closure of your case, it's your intention to have a clean slate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And I know Ms. Davis is working on that as well as other folks. As -- and I -- she will have one more witness, and then she has to unfortunately go back to the law firm that so nicely loaned her to us for a long while. But I know we will have that -- definitely an answer for you very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, who will deal with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So I understand there's some protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. This witness is currently in the ICTY witness protection programme, and the protection officer has asked me to -- for security purposes to have face distortion and pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the witness is aware of that and agrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there's no objections from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it's necessary, but I'm hardly in the position to object, Your Honour. And I think as the evidence comes out of this witness, I think it will be clear why this gentleman should not be given any protective measures and be testifying open, in public, so the public knows who he is and what he has to say. But I understand the measures, and I accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Of course, Mr. Karnavas, the Bench has the power to lift the protective measures at a later stage, if the situation requires. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have the same position as the Defence of Mr. Blagojevic. In principle, at this point, I don't know to what effect this is useful, but bearing in mind the contents of his testimony, I think you will be in a position to judge as to the necessity of these protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that the request for the protective measures is granted. Could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Could you take a look at a piece of paper which has been marked Prosecution 671, and could you tell us if that's your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you give us the month and year of your birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us briefly what schooling you went to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went to the secondary mechanical engineering school, and then I started energetics and attended (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you do any regular JNA service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in what years?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And after your service in the JNA, did you retain a connection with the JNA in a reserve status?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was part of the reserve force assigned to the iron works factory (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was your particular rank when you left your JNA active service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: When I left my active service, I had a rank of (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were you promoted through the reserve ranks --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the rank of (redacted).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: By 1992, the spring of 1992, what was your reserve rank in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: My rank was that of a reserve (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And with the outbreak of the war in Bosnia, did you become a member of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what unit in the VRS did you first become a member of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I first became a member of the (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And by July 1995, were you in the security branch of

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in the time period of the fall of Srebrenica, were you involved in the murder operation to kill thousands of Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to skip ahead in time and go to some of the post-war facts in this case. And can you tell me, (redacted) did you apply in Belgrade to immigrate to the United States?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you make a false statement on your immigration form there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was that false statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I did not make a statement regarding my participation in the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And pursuant to that application to enter the U.S., did you -- were you able -- and your family able to immigrate to the U.S.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And about what month did you arrive in the U.S.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell me what the name of that lawyer is?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to consult with him prior to testifying today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you understand by testifying today that you did have a right to have a lawyer present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you speak with your lawyer about his potential presence today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I talked to him, and I told him that his presence was not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And do you understand that what you say today can be used against you later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That if you don't -- that you do have a right not to say anything at all. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Getting back to your entry into the United States,(redacted) (redacted), did you fill out an application for permanent residence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't mean to interrupt the flow. I would like the gentleman to be aware of the maximum penalty at this time as a result of his involvement. I know that he understands that he may be charged and I think it may be necessary for him to understand the penalty that he is facing, because of his right to have a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What do you mean by the maximum penalties?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, as I understand the gentleman did participate directly, as we will hear, in the killings in -- I believe it was in -- perhaps not in Branjevo Farm directly, but in one of the other locations. So I would imagine that the maximum penalty he is facing is life imprisonment. And I think that he does need to be aware of that, that that's what he's subject to in the event he goes forward with testifying and that he's waiving his rights to have his lawyer present knowingly and voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I know (redacted) is a fine lawyer and I'm sure has discussed these matters with him. I can clarify that without any problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you understand that if indicted and convicted for crimes involving the murder of Muslim men after the fall of Srebrenica, you could face a penalty up to life imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you been aware of that in your dealings with the Prosecution since you've had your lawyer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then getting back to the U.S. And in April --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey. I have to remind you that this witness under the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't think this is a problem. There's many folks in the U.S. from the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't mean that. You may continue, maybe somebody in your team will look into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I understand and I understand the problem. And I will fix it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Back to the U.S., in April did you apply to register as a permanent resident in the U.S.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In those applications, were you asked the same question about your military service while living in Bosnia or the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as you had in Belgrade, did you make a false statement by failing to mention your VRS deployment during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. In August of 2002, were you interviewed by the OTP at the town where you were living in the United States regarding the Srebrenica events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was an agent from the FBI present during some of those contacts and interviews?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In that August 2002 interview with the OTP, did you acknowledge that you were -- you took part at the murder operation at Orahovac on July 14th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did the FBI interview regarding any potential false statements on immigration documents to the United States at that same time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And during that interview with the FBI, did you admit to them that you had failed to mention your service in the VRS, thereby making -- admitting making a false statement to the U.S. Immigration authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you also testify in a deposition at the United States attorney's office in the town where you were living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you repeat your question. I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Did you go to the United States attorney's office in August of 2002 and answer questions from me in a deposition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in that deposition you were under oath. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you acknowledge your responsibility in Orahovac during that deposition -- or acknowledge your involvement in, excuse me, in Orahovac in that deposition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And at about that time did you agree to cooperate with the Office of the Prosecutor and promise to testify and tell the truth in any future proceedings that we would ask you to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did the Office of the Prosecutor promise to protect you and your family and have you apply to the witness protection programme, if it was -- became necessary, for example, if you were deported from the United States?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did the -- did myself or anyone from the Office of the Prosecutor make any promises to you regarding whether or not you would be charged by anyone, the United States or the Office of the Prosecutor or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: As you sit here today, has anyone made any promises to you about whether or not you will be prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: On 1 April 2003, were you not indicted on four counts of false statements to immigration authorities by the United States government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you were arrested and incarcerated in -- at that time as well, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And on July 2nd, 2003, did you plead guilty to two counts of providing a false statement on the immigration applications?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did one of those counts involve the false statement in Belgrade and the other involve the false statement in the U.S. that we've spoken of earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And on 24 October 2003, were you and your family deported from the United States back to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how much time did you serve in gaol in the United States?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Less than seven months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And precisely how much, as you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: From the 2nd of April, 2003, until the 23rd of October, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And upon entering Bosnia, were you and your family -- did you take the protection of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Recently, on 3 December, did you provide information to Alistair Graham and myself, where you denied knowing Mr. Beara or knowing anything about Mr. Beara and the events of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you in addition say that you did not know anything about what triage meant, or something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At the end of that statement, did the OTP insist that you be provided with a lawyer by the Registry of this institution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did the OTP explain to you that they did not believe you were telling the truth about Mr. Beara and triage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you spoken to the Office of the Prosecutor more recently on 21 January 2004 and provided another statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you admit in that statement that some of the information you had provided earlier was not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us now in particular what information you provided that was not true.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Regarding the 21st, is that correct? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Regarding the December 3rd statement to Mr. Graham and myself regarding Beara, triage, and other things.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: On the 2nd of December, I said that I did not know Beara and I did not know anything about the triage and that I did not have any information as to whether Beara was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were those statements true or false?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: They were false.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And as we go over the events, I'll have you explain those in more detail. Did you recently, on 21 January, provide another -- or acknowledge you had made another false statement regarding your time at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you briefly tell us what the false statement is and what the reality is in fact.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: At that meeting, I said that I had not been at that time part of the operation to kill and execute Muslims in Srebrenica; whereas, in the actual fact, I had spent the entire evening until the morning hours when I had left. After the operation of the execution was completed, I spent the entire time in the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Had you earlier in your deposition in your first statement told the Office of the Prosecutor that you were involved in securing prisoners at Orahovac and aware of the executions, but you had left right after the executions had started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And now you're telling us that you stayed throughout the period of the executions all night and into the next day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go back to the time when you came into the Zvornik Brigade. You said you were assigned to one of the battalions. Can you briefly describe to us your advancement in the Zvornik Brigade from the time you first came in, until July 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The first unit I belonged to in the VRS was the 3rd Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade, located in Kiseljak. I was in an infantry company, together with Srecko Maksimovic [as interpreted]. It was up until the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry. Could you say who were -- who the battalion person was you were with was again. I'm not sure the name was correct or they may not have heard it correctly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Srecko Acimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So it's Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was Srecko Acimovic to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: We worked together in the company and in the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And is Acimovic spelled with an "A"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Keep going. Tell us about your career, up till July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: (redacted). And then I learned that people who were interested in it could attend training in Pancevo, people in the brigade who were interested in it. And upon completion of that training, they could regulate their status in the units of the VRS. So I applied for that post; it was approved. And I was told that I would then be transferred to the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade. And in the Zvornik Brigade, I was in the security organ until my status was resolved and until I was to be sent to undergo training. And since this did not happen, I received my appointment in the Zvornik Brigade headquarters as the security officer of the Zvornik Brigade. My activities in that time consisted of tasks involving tours of the defence lines, where units were, monitoring the work of the observation posts that were manned by the personnel from the unit, dispatching daily reports, being on duty, and all the usual tasks as needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who was your immediate superior in the security branch of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In the security organ, the chief was Dragan Nikolic. He was the chief of the security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in July of 1995, what was -- what was Dragan Nikolic's rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He had the rank of a lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in July of 1995, what was your rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In 1995, I was a reserve captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you explain how a lieutenant can be a superior to a captain in that particular context.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic was an officer of the JNA, and I was -- I am a reserve officer. And that is the difference in the appointment that one can receive and in the treatment of the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, as Drago Nikolic as your superior, were you -- did you have to follow his orders, or as a captain, could you give him orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I had to follow his orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And who, if you know, did Drago Nikolic report to? Who was his most immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: His immediate superior was the chief of the security in the Drina Corps command, and that would be Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in the command of the Zvornik Brigade, did Mr. Nikolic have a superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. That was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, that was Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe the relationship, the official relationship, between Vinko Pandurevic and Drago Nikolic. Were there any problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. There would be problems from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And could you give us an example of some of those problems or one of those problems.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Well, in terms of reports and the use of vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The manner in which reports were sent and the use of vehicles. Drago wanted the vehicles to be used and controlled only by the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, up until the period of July 1995, were you aware of the command of the Zvornik Brigade being involved in the murder of any prisoners within the custody of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know the command was aware of those -- murder of prisoners, and I'm talking about prior to the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It was because the superiors themselves said that they should -- that these people should be taken away and executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How do you know the superiors themselves said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Because when the security chief came from the briefing, he gave the order for this task to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And are you talking about Drago Nikolic coming from the meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what meetings are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That was the regular morning meeting or briefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was at that regular morning briefing, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The commander, the chiefs of the staffs and of various sections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you ever at one of those meetings when such an order was given?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No, not when that order was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may object at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, I don't know what the relevancy is with all of this with respect to what happened prior to the fall of Srebrenica. The indictments don't cover any of that period. Second of all, unless I'm mistaken, I don't have any disclosure material with respect to this. Granted it's talking about Zvornik. But I'm somewhat concerned that perhaps the Prosecutor is trying to suggest that the commands at all of the brigades were engaged in murder operations prior to Srebrenica, and they're using this gentleman here as a vehicle for establishing that. I don't know. I just don't know what disclosure material they're relying on, and I don't know what the relevancy is with respect to the charges of these two individuals that are standing before this particular Trial Bench, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, would you please make some clarification of this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This is a point that the witness has told us from the very beginning and is part of the discovery material. I'm -- It's my intention in this direct to try to bring out most of the important points that this witness has said that shows his knowledge, his potential involvement, the knowledge and potential involvement of others, especially those that have testified in this case. Because I do not want to be left -- leave anyone with the impression that we are trying to not provide the information that may affect this witness, or Mr. Obrenovic, or anyone else. And this is a statement that he has told us from early on, has been part of the record early on, and it is something that I will deal with very quickly and go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed, but you have to remember that those periods were not covered by the indictment, unless you want to establish a kind of consistency practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I really don't intend anything that formal, Mr. President. And I -- but it was just one of the facts he's always testified to, and I just thought we should bring it up. I won't, obviously, cover everything that he's mentioned because it's too voluminous and not particularly on point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's get to July 1995, and -- in fact, let's go right to the 13th of July, 1995. Can you tell us what particular job you recall that day and what you did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, 1995, in the afternoon, the duty officer of the Zvornik Brigade tasked me with escorting a convoy of humanitarian aid from the Russian Battalion to Bratunac, and to hand them over to the security organ in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you go with that convoy to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, after I received the orders, together with the driver of the security organ, Milorad Bircakovic. I was in a vehicle with him and we drove on the old macadam road to Bratunac. And in front of the brigade command, which was indicated to me by Bircakovic, because that was the first time I was there, I didn't where it was, we checked with Momir Nikolic where the security organ of the Bratunac Brigade was. After we were told that he was not there and that his whereabouts were unknown to the people we talked to, the leader of the convoy demanded that I continue to escort the convoy down to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What kind of vehicle were you in with the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I was with the driver in an Opel Rekord, it's called Rekord and it was an estate wagon which was dark green in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you go to Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. Pursuant to the request of the convoy leader for us to escort him to Potocari, we continued on. We arrived in Potocari. They parked their vehicles, and the convoy leader told me to wait there until he sorted things out regarding the convoy and until he did all the things that he had to do in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was in his convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly, but I was told it was humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was this a United States or an UNPROFOR convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It was a UN convoy of the Russian Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, where -- about what time did you get to the Potocari area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I can't tell exactly. Four or five hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you give us a rough idea what time of day this is, morning, afternoon, evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It was at dusk, in the early evening, at around 4.00 or 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And can you describe what hour in Potocari you were, what kind of buildings, any bases around, anything that -- any landmarks you can give us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I was on some kind of a plateau in Potocari in front of the place where the peacekeeping battalion, it was the Dutch Battalion, was located. I saw that there were many women, children, men there, men in uniforms. And at one point, I saw Momir Nikolic. I knew him, I recognised him, because he had come to see Drago Nikolic in the Zvornik Brigade command one or two times. I spent some time with him, very briefly. I just said hello, and I asked him, since that was my first time there, who these people were, what was happening there. He told me that they were Muslims from Srebrenica there, members of the Republika Srpska Army. And he also told me -- I saw the other part of the civilian population, and they told me that they were waiting to be transported to leave to the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina through Tuzla. I also saw many trucks on that plateau. I asked him how come that there were so many trucks, and he told me that this was organised and that they came from the whole of the Republika Srpska and that they were all gathered here to be used for the transportation purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell -- was there anybody with Momir Nikolic when you were there in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: At that time when we spoke, nobody else was there. Later on, because I had my duties related to the convoy, I had to go and check the progress of the unloading of the convoy and the takeover of the goods. But I saw at one point that he was present there and that he was talking to somebody, although I don't know who he was talking to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what -- after talking with Momir Nikolic, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: After talking with him, I went to meet with the convoy leader, because I wanted him to give me further information as to what we were to do. Since I had done everything I had to do, I escorted the convoy to the place that they requested, from Zvornik to Potocari. Since he was unable to sort out his stay there, I don't know who he had been talking to, and to sort out everything about the unloading and takeover of the humanitarian aid he had brought there, he asked me to escort him. He said that we were to return to Bratunac. Immediately after receiving this request, I and the driver returned immediately to Bratunac. When we came to a building, I was told that this was the town hall in Bratunac. It was in the evening. A person was present there. They demanded that a representative of the municipality come. They wanted to talk to that person and to organise the delivery of the humanitarian aid they had brought with them. I don't know how long it took for that person to arrive. I also don't know who that person was. But at any rate, we entered this building. We went into an office, sat down with them, dinner was ordered, because we had already spent a long time on this trip. They continued discussing the organisation and the unloading and the takeover of the humanitarian aid. They also discussed the possibility of doing all that as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So how long did you actually stay in Bratunac dealing with this -- these convoy issues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I remained in Bratunac for an hour, an hour and a half, two hours. Later on I asked -- I told the convoy leader that I could not wait anymore, and asked for his permission to leave to report to the Zvornik Brigade command, because I could not see when this would end. He approved this, and I went on with my driver, Bircakovic, along the same road we took on our way from Zvornik there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you describe where the route you said this macadam road took.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: This macadam road went along Drinjaca. That was my first time there because I'm not from that region, and it was quite strange to me and the road itself was in really bad condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You say along the Drinjaca River or is that what you said? I'm not clear on the translation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It was moving across the Drinjaca. There is a larger area that is referred to as "Drinjaca." I'm not exactly sure where the river goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you aware of the main road between Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, and Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I was aware of one other road, but at the time we headed out when we escorted the convoy, the leader requested that we should take that particular road. I don't know why. On the way back, I said, Bircakovic, since it is getting dark, I don't want to experiment with new roads, could you please take me along the same road we had taken so that I could get to the Zvornik Brigade headquarters as soon as possible and to report on the assignment that I had completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you get back to the Zvornik Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And about what time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Sometime in the evening hours, at about 10.00 or 11.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what happened when you got back to the Zvornik Brigade headquarters? I guess this is 10.00 or 11.00 in the evening, the night of 13 July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, it was. I went in. I got into the compound of the Zvornik Brigade headquarters. Drago Nikolic was in front of the reception desk, the security chief of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the last sentence the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was said, if anything, when you came in and you saw Drago Nikolic there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Drago said, Where have you been all this time? I needed the vehicle. Get ready, together with Jasikovac. And then he selected a couple of members of the military police. He said that the vehicle would be secured for us to go to Orahovac. A bus with Muslims from Srebrenica in coming, and you have to organise the accommodation for those people in the elementary school building in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who is Jasikovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Jasikovac was the commander of the military police company in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you see anybody, any other officers around the area, while you were at the Zvornik Brigade command that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And after receiving this order from Drago Nikolic, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Together with Jasikovac, the military police company commander and five or six other military police, in a -- we went to Orahovac in a military police van.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And about what time did you get to the school at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Well, let me see. It was in the evening, between 11.00 and midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did Drago Nikolic go with you to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No, he didn't. However, he came later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, when he gave you that order to go to Orahovac, what was your understanding as to what your job was in relation to this Orahovac and the Muslim prisoners arriving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: My understanding was that my task would be to organise accommodation for the Muslims from Srebrenica, who were taken to the hall of the elementary school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That evening, did you have an opinion on what you thought was going to happen to those Muslims, prisoners at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Well, I had my assumptions. After all, it was war time and I thought they would be first accommodated in the school and then that they would be executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why would you have thought they would be executed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: If they were not going to be executed, then they wouldn't keep them there. They would have then transported them to the requested destinations, that is, to the areas in the direction of Tuzla, to the exit points.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when Mr. Graham and myself first saw you in the United States, did you tell us the same thing about your opinion that you've just stated now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What happened when you got to the school at Orahovac with these MPs?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'd like to correct the record. That's not exactly what the gentleman said. It misstates his prior testimony. If Mr. McCloskey wishes to vouch for his previous testimony, which is improper in my opinion at this stage, at least he should show him what he has stated. Because my recollection is that he stated that he thought that they were going to be executed once he saw that some of their belongings were taken away, and that gave him the impression. Because they had to drop off their belongings before they went in. So it's slightly different. And the only reason I'm making the point is I don't think we can say, Well, since he said it back then and he's saying now, that it must be correct. If he's testifying from his independent memory I don't have a problem with that. If Mr. McCloskey wishes to refresh the memory, that's fine. But to vouch, I think, is improper. To say he said it back then, he's saying it now, therefore it must be true. I can only suspect this is being done because the gentleman has given variations of his testimony and has given false information prior to the arrangement that he's currently made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe this issue is a very good point during your cross-examination. Here I don't think the Prosecution would like to go deeper into this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honour, but I would prefer that the Prosecutor not say, Did you say -- tell us that back then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it does not naturally mean that it must be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. But if he's going to say what he said back then, at least give him -- he can say the whole thing what he said back then, which was in addition to the fact that they were -- some of their belongings were being taken away. It's a minor point and I know that Mr. McCloskey doesn't mean anything by just -- he's probably trying to shortcut the process. But I would prefer that we just get his independent memory here, as opposed to saying, Well, did you tell us that back then, unless he's going to be impeaching him. Then I don't have a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's leave it for your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's a very good subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I think it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think you're correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, let's have our break. We'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Witness, just going back to when Drago Nikolic told you about the Muslims coming and you to go to Orahovac, did he give you any idea how many Muslims were -- would be coming to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At that time did you -- had you received any information from any sources about Muslim prisoners anywhere in Zvornik or the Bratunac areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you -- when Drago Nikolic was giving you this information at the brigade headquarters, did you see any officers around before you left for Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you said you went with some MPs in a van. What happened when you got to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: We got to Orahovac. We went to the football pitch just outside the elementary school in Orahovac. Shortly after that, buses started arriving and in the meantime Jasikovac, the military police commander, deployed military police members who had arrived to the entrance into the gym. And the buses carrying Muslims from Srebrenica came closer, close to the entrance, and then the doors would be open. Jasikovac came back. They -- he told them to get inside the gym as quickly as possible, to take off their coats, and get inside the gym of the elementary school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were you the superior of Jasikovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Well, I was the security officer, and Drago was superior to Jasikovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, you were a captain at the time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So who was the senior officer in charge at Orahovac that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That night Drago Nikolic came to the gym after the Muslims had been put up in the school gym. He said that there were more buses coming. Those people would be put up in the elementary school in Petkovci, Orahovac, and Pilica. He didn't stay there very long. And together with the driver, Milorad Bircakovic, he left. He didn't say where he was going.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And when Drago wasn't at the school, who was in charge at the school, what VRS soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Me and Jasikovac, the MP commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We've heard a lot about the unity of command in this job. Was there one person that was in overall command or did you share command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Jasikovac worked with and was superior to the military police. And I was involved in organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was your military authority in relation to Jasikovac? Could you give him orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No, I actually couldn't. Drago Nikolic could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what was -- what were you doing there that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: My duty was to organise and secure accommodation for Srebrenica Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when did you form the opinion that these Muslims were going to be killed, in relation to the events you've just -- you've been describing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I drew this conclusion on the 14th, after the arrival of Drago Nikolic in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was it that caused you to draw that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: With the arrival of Drago Nikolic in Orahovac sometime in the evening of the 14th, I learned from him that those people, those Srebrenica Muslims, were going to be executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: After he arrived, I first asked him where he had been so far, because we were having problems there. And he said that Beara had come in the meantime, that he had things to do, that he did not have time to come earlier. He wanted to know where Jasikovac was so that we could start organising things. He also said we needed to find volunteers for the actual execution of these Muslims from Srebrenica. The force engineers received their assignment. And he said, We should proceed immediately with the preparations and the actual execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. About what time of day did Nikolic tell you about these -- the actual executions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: This was late in the afternoon, maybe in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: On the 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, on the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I want -- haven't gotten quite there yet, I want to take us back to the late night hours of the 13th, the early morning hours of the 14th when you actually go to the school at Orahovac and the Muslims arrive. Can you tell us about what time the Muslims first started arriving.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: At about 12.00 hours that night, in the evening of the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Around midnight of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did you have an opinion when the Muslims arrived at Orahovac what was going to happen to them before Drago actually told you this on the day of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to the form of the question. He can ask if he knew what would happen, what was going to happen, which goes to knowledge, versus asking for speculative opinions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think the word is misused. Do you have an opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you asking an opinion of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely. What he thought was going to happen to the Muslims that night, because it's unfortunately been confused. I'm asking him what he thought. I think it's the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You've testified earlier about what you thought was going to happen to the Muslims. When did you first think that they were going to be executed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Immediately after going to Orahovac and upon receiving the assignment to put up those Muslims in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Like you -- that's basically what you testified earlier to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. When did you know for a fact they were going to be executed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In the evening of the 14th of July, when Drago Nikolic, the chief security officer of the Zvornik Brigade, arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after the Muslims start arriving around midnight, as you've said, did Drago Nikolic come back to Orahovac any time that early morning hours of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So can you tell us what happened from about 12.00 midnight until, you know, until dawn on the -- during the 14th? What was going on at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Mostly members of the military police of the Zvornik Brigade, they were involved in the security. I was on a clearing outside at the school gym where the Srebrenica Muslims were accommodated. At the time, there were no major problems. No one came -- I mean, none of the officers, after the visit of Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm still about -- I haven't gotten beyond the morning of the 14th, about 8.00 a.m. So until what hours on the 14th did Muslims continue to arrive at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: They stopped arriving in the school sometime during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, during the day of the 14th, did any Muslims arrive at the school in Orahovac, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And roughly how many Muslims do you recall arriving to Orahovac total?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In my assessment, between 5 and 600.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where were they put?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: They were placed in the gym of the Orahovac elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What happened during the daylight hours at the school at Orahovac on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when it was. It could have been sometime in the afternoon. I was not present at the entrance to the gym, but I know that two Srebrenica Muslims were taken out - in what manner, I'm not able to tell you. They had a disagreement with -- a fight with two soldiers, including Jasikovac. And I saw that one of the two was killed on this plateau, this clearing, outside the gym. I didn't see the other, but Jasikovac later told me that there was one more killed. This all happened at the time I was coming back from the telephone call which I had made with Mr. Jokic, who was the duty operations officer. I talked to him because I wanted to know where Drago Nikolic was and whether he could provide assistance in terms of security in Orahovac. And thereafter, he made a telephone conversation with Lazar Ristic, the deputy commander of the infantry battalion, to see if there were troops that could be sent to reinforce the security needed at the Orahovac elementary school gym where the Muslims were being kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let us first finish the incident related to the Muslims who were killed. Did you actually see a Muslim killed outside the gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was -- did this appear to be justified or an unjustified killing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Unjustified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who killed this Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't know which one of the members of this group did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Which group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The group of people who were there with him, the members of the military police who were with Jasikovac at the MP commander [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You said before you had seen this murder, you had decided to go call the duty officer of the brigade. And can you explain to us why you decided to go call the brigade duty officer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I decided to do that because I thought that we might encounter major problems there, and I wanted to know if there was any possibility of sending more people to reinforce security. And I wanted Drago Nikolic to be notified of these problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What problems did you think you were going to have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know to what extent it was possible for those prisoners to get out. Given the number of people, I thought that it was impossible to provide adequate security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So where did you go to make a telephone call?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went to a private house in the vicinity of the elementary school. I don't know the name of the owner of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who did you call?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I called the duty officer, the operations duty officer, of the Zvornik Brigade, Mr. Jokic. And I told him I needed help. If possible, if he was able to organise it, to send me some help. I wanted to know if Drago was there, to -- I wanted to talk to him. I wanted him to call me or to come over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you say "him," meaning who? Drago Nikolic or Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I said whether Drago Nikolic was there, and that if he was there, that he should send him over to Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how did you know that you were talking to Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: At first, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then how was it that you knew who you were talking to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: On the basis of my recollection that this could be Jokic, and then I realised it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember an investigator in the U.S. Reminding you of any names of people or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did that help you identify who you were speaking to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, as you sit here today, is there any doubt in your mind who you were talking to when you were talking to the duty officer that day on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did Mr. Jokic say to you when you made this request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He said he didn't know where Drago was, and that they didn't know what the possibility was, because they did not have any men available there at the time, but that he would see what he could do and that he would do his best to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. After that did you call anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I already said that I had talked to Lazar Ristic, the deputy commander of the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe you testified earlier that you said that Dragan Jokic called Lazar Ristic. Perhaps it was a translation issue, but can you clarify that for us. Did you call Lazar Ristic or did Jokic call Lazar Ristic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No. I called Lazar Ristic, after I finished my conversation with Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know about what time during the day you called Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact time, but I know that it was sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And how soon after calling Mr. Jokic did you call Mr. Ristic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Immediately after the first phone call, I called Mr. Ristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who, to your knowledge, at the time was Mr. Ristic? Why would you call Mr. Ristic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Mr. Ristic was the deputy commander of the 4th Battalion, and the 4th Battalion, its headquarters and its defence lines, were located slightly closer to the location of the elementary school where the Muslims were housed. And the reason was that if he had any people to provide for us to assist us, they would have been able to arrive more quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so what did you say to -- and who was Lazar Ristic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Lazar Ristic was the deputy commander of the 4th Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did you say to Mr. Ristic when you called him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I told him that I was in the school where the Muslims from Srebrenica were housed and that there were not enough people to provide security and that we would need, if he had, any people available, that he should send them over to assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He said that at that time he didn't know to what extent he would be able to assist us, because they themselves also had certain precaution measures that they had to take in their part of the line, but that he would do as much as he could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So at the time in the afternoon of these phone calls, is there anybody else at Orahovac, besides the Muslims you've described and the MPs you've described with Jasikovac and yourself? Any other military or police units, or any other units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. They were present there, but I don't know exactly, because I don't know them. They had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Besides the MPs and yourself, who else was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: They were only providing security. In fact, as for the security, there were only the MPs and us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So let me clarify it. Are you saying there are some other troops besides the MPs and yourself that were at the school at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Only later did I see that there were some, but not at the time when we were providing security. But after the request was issued, personnel came from the Zvornik Brigade command. A group came. I don't know exactly how many there were, I think maybe five or six. And among them --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell me how long after your phone call with Mr. Jokic these people from the command showed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may have been about --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The question was -- the answer -- the question was: After the phone call with Mr. Jokic, these people from the command. I'm not quite sure that the gentleman -- I withdraw the objection, Your Honour. I see that he did indicate that they came from the command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the answer is that, but after the request was issued, personnel came from the Zvornik Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Witness, so how long after the phone call to Mr. Jokic did these people from the Zvornik command show up at the school at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Approximately an hour later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how is it -- or why is it that you conclude they were from the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I concluded that because I knew two of them personally, two of the people in the group, that was Sretan Milosevic, Captain Sretan Milosevic, assistant commander for logistics in the Zvornik Brigade, and Milenko Jovanovic, he was the commander of the headquarters administration in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was his rank, Milenko's rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. He may have been a sergeant. I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were these people from the brigade command assigned responsibility at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. They immediately started providing security for the Muslims that were housed in the elementary school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who told them what to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Milosevic immediately said that he would help with the organisation, because he had learned that there were problems here. And Milenko simply joined in organising things, together with Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you help organise this security also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did anybody show up from the 4th Battalion, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, it was a group of about four, five, or maybe six soldiers. I don't recall exactly, not more than that. Because he immediately told me during the conversation I had with Lazar Ristic, that's what he told me then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When did the people from the 4th Battalion show up, how long after your phone call with Ristic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Well, according to my estimate, as far as I can remember, about two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people from the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How do you know they were from the 4th Battalion, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I assumed that on the basis of the request that had been made and the size of the group that had arrived, their strength.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Which direction did they arrive from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: They arrived from the direction of Kitovnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that the direction of the front lines where most of the 4th Battalion troops were deployed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. That's where the defence line manned by the 4th Battalion was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. After your phone calls, did you phone anybody else besides Dragan Jokic and Lazar Ristic that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And besides the people from the headquarters who you've described and the people from the 4th Battalion, did any other officers come to the Orahovac school after you made those phone calls?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When -- didn't you say to us that at some point Drago Nikolic arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic arrived in the early evening on the 14th of July, immediately before the beginning of the execution of the prisoners from Srebrenica. I thought that you were referring to the group that had arrived, if somebody had arrived at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. What I mean is after the afternoon after these phone calls, when was the next group of officers that arrived, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. Drago Nikolic came. The chief of security for the Drina Corps, Popovic, arrived. They came together in a -- in the same vehicle. And I didn't see any other officer there, any other officer arriving there or being present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And about what time did Drago Nikolic and Popovic arrive at the school at Orahovac on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In the early evening, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Prior to their arrival, had there been any executions of prisoners in the gym, aside from the killings that you've already mentioned that you saw the one person killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Prior to Drago Nikolic and Popovic arriving, had you or anyone else provided any plan to kill those people in the gym?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what happened -- what was -- what happened when Drago and Popovic show up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: When Drago Nikolic arrived, I was en route, on the road, on the path between the gym and the private house, that was the path that led to Kitovnice. I said to him, Where have you been? There have been problems here, something to that effect. He told me that Beara had come and that he had things to do with him, that he was unable to come earlier. He asked about what kind of problems there were, and he said, All of these people are to be executed immediately. Where is Jasikovac? Do we have to ask for volunteers to organise this. The engineer unit received its orders, and we have to prepare the vehicles immediately and the volunteers for the people to be taken out, put on to vehicles, and taken to the execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, when you spoke to the OTP in the United States, you never mentioned anything about engineers at this stage of the story, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you or did you not mention engineers in your story in the United States?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you didn't mention anything about engineers in the United States. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And why are you now mentioning engineers? Why did you -- I'm sorry. Let me try that again. Why did you not mention engineers when you were talking about this information in the United States?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. That was the beginning of my direct involvement and responsibility for this operation that was carried out. I left out some things because I was afraid of incurring this responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Afraid of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I was afraid that an indictment would be issued against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So -- now, describe how this was the beginning of your personal responsibility. How did that relate to the engineers, in your view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I had contacts with the engineers about the relocation of the mass graves and the entire operation in which the mass graves were relocated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not talking about the relocation of the mass graves. Right now you've mentioned that Drago Nikolic mentioned something about the engineers at Orahovac. Did you have any dealings with the engineers while you were at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what did you mean when you said Drago said the engineers had their responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I was told that they were preparing to dig the pits where the Muslims that would be executed would be buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So why didn't you tell us that information in the United States?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I said -- as I said, that marks the beginning of my involvement with the engineer unit, my responsibility and my direct involvement in these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Can you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: So for reasons of my personal safety and the safety of my family that lives in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So after Drago Nikolic told you this information, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
