utterances.text: I immediately started preparing the vehicles and preparing for the prisoners to be taken out -- I mean, the prisoners who were then sent to the execution sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did you do to prepare vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Vehicles were brought and parked in front of the very entrance to the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What kind of vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: These were the vehicles from the Zvornik Brigade, and they had the part of the truck was covered with canvas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who arranged for these vehicles to come to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I assumed that it was Drago Nikolic, together with the assistant to the commander for logistics, Sretan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you have anything to do with ordering or speaking to anyone about getting trucks over to the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there any material brought to blindfold the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know who arranged for acquiring the material for the blindfolds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That was Jasikovac, the commander of the military police company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did he get for blindfolds and where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there, so I don't know who he talked to. But at any rate, the materials were brought in and the military police officers cut the material into required lengths.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know any particular officers by name that took part in this making of the blindfolds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't know the officers, but I do know that Nada, the police woman, whose last name I don't know, was there. She was a member of the military police company of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Besides Nada, were there any other female MPs that were at Orahovac that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So as you're organising the trucks and the MPs are organising the blindfolds, what else is going on, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In that period, also the volunteers who would carry out the executions were also being prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was preparing the volunteers or calling for the volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic and Jasikovac, the military police company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know who volunteered for this job or who was chosen or volunteered for this job, the execution job, that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know what units they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, what happens next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Muslims were taken out of the school; they were blindfolded. And they got on the trucks. And as soon as a truck would be full, it would set off towards its destination, the place where the Srebrenica Muslims were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know who picked out those execution sites?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I assume it was Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why do you assume it was him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Because he told me that these people would be executed, and he went to that area, to the area where the executions were carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How do you know he went to the area where the executions were carried out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I know because when the volunteers were picked out and when the vehicles went, he went there personally. He was not at the place where I was, where the organisation was carried out, where the exits of the prisoners from the gym and their entry into the vehicles and the arrival of new vehicles after the full vehicles had left, when all this was organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. When the first vehicles full of Muslim prisoners drove away from the school, did you hear any gunfire after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. There were bursts of gunfire from the direction in which they had gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how long did this process of blindfolding, loading prisoners, and taking them out to the execution sites go on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It took the entire evening of the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how about the morning -- the early morning hours of the 15th? What was done from midnight on the 15th to daybreak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: After the Muslims were executed, the cleanup operation was carried out, the areas where they were located were cleaned up. Items of clothing or footwear or documents that remained there were cleaned up. This was organised by Jasikovac, the commander of the military police company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And had any Muslims died in the gym while they were staying there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. I think about a dozen of them had also -- were also taken to the execution site and were buried there in the mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. About what time of night was the last truck of Muslims loaded and sent off to the execution sites?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It may have been at around 4.00 or 5.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The morning of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you do after the last of the Muslims were sent off to the execution site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I was present there while the place was cleaned up, and I waited to go to the brigade because of the vehicles and all those people who had to go there. But at any rate, I did not have any specific tasks that I had to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your task to get the Muslims loaded on the trucks had already finished. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, during the day of the 14th or the early morning hours of the 15th, did you see any excavation or engineering equipment in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you ever get involved in organising for heavy equipment to come bury the bodies at the mass graves near Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know who did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. It was the engineer unit of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But do you know who contacted them to get them involved in this mess?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And about what time were you able to leave the school at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It was approximately sometime in the morning at around 8.00 in the morning on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And prior to you leaving, did you notice if any of the MPs were allowed to leave before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I didn't notice any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you notice whether or not Nada was allowed to leave at any time during this process, the one female MP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't notice that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A slight qualification to the question. Was allowed to leave, as if someone was compelling them to stay. I think the question should be rephrased whether she left, as opposed to being allowed to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's a very minor, very minor issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is, but it's suggestive. I want a clean record. Mr. McCloskey continuously argues against me for trying to muddy up the waters with respect to the record. And I'm trying to just make sure we have a clean record here, because it may become an issue at some other point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you insist. Mr. McCloskey, would you please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know if Nada, the female MP, ever left the area of Orahovac after this -- after you saw her with the blindfold?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Soldiers are generally not allowed to leave assignments; they have to get instructions before they go. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So did you receive any instructions from anyone allowing you to go or leave Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. From Drago Nikolic, he told us that we were allowed to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what time did Drago Nikolic tell you you were allowed to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I can't be specific about the time, but it was in the morning after the execution was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where was he when he told you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: On the clearing in front of the gym where the Muslims had been housed, I mean the elementary school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And so where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went to the Zvornik Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And why did you go to the command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went to the command to go on my way, because I -- it was not my intention to stay there for any length of time. Because the vehicles went only as far as the Zvornik Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, why in particular did you go to the Zvornik Brigade command? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went to the command just to accompany the group. I mean, I went there because of the availability of the transport. My intention was to continue on my way home from there, because prior to that I had been allowed by Drago Nikolic to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. In the United States you told us that Drago allowed you to leave shortly after you heard the executions starting out at the killing fields, and was that true when you told us that in the U.S.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was that a truthful statement in the U.S., that you were allowed to leave at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection because -- okay. He gave a false statement in the United States; he does admit to it. But now the question was he allowed to leave is suggesting that he requested to leave and he was not permitted to leave. As I understand it when he corrected himself and in telling the truth, at no time did he indicate that he wanted to leave, that he made a request to leave, and he was forbidden to leave. There lies the difference. I don't think -- you know, if the question was rephrased, such as: Did you try to leave before the executions or right after the executions and he said yes, then we can follow on with the next question. But there is no indication from the witness that at any point in time once the executions started did he ever asked Drago Nikolic to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think the problem here is about the time, not about whether he's allowed and he asked any permission to leave after the starting of the killings. But anyway, Mr. McCloskey, try to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In the United States you told us about being present when men were loaded on to the trucks and sent to the execution site. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you also told us that before you left Orahovac, you were able to hear the sound of executions down the road from the school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, in the United States, just can you briefly tell us what version you gave us in the United States about when you left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In the United States I said that I had left after the third or -- the second or the third truckload of Muslims who were to be executed, in Orahovac, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was that false?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is the truth what you have told us about today, that you in fact left in the morning of the 15th, after the job was finished?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And -- now, let's get back to -- you went by the headquarters briefly, and then where did you go, this is on the morning of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: After that, I went home to Kozluk, which is located some 30 kilometres from the Zvornik Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. How long were you at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters the morning of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Two hours, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went home to my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. I mean where did you go in the Zvornik Brigade headquarters when you were there? In fact, let me start over, because I think we might have some confusion. How long were you actually at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters the morning of the 15th when you stopped by after Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: For about two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And where on the premises of the Zvornik Brigade did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went to the premises of the Zvornik Brigade command, where we had an office; I mean we, the security branch. I didn't stay there very long, because I had to go home. So I actually spent more time outside the building trying to figure out how I can get home, what transport I could get.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: While you were at the premises of the Zvornik Brigade, did you see Drago Nikolic there that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No, I was not with Drago Nikolic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you ever see him around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: While you were at the brigade that morning, did you see Dragan Obrenovic around the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How about Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Popovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Beara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Any officers you recall seeing while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And why was it you went home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went home to see my family, because I had been absent for some time. I don't know exactly for how long. Because on that day they were supposed to leave this place and go on a vacation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when you got home, did you see your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So how long did you stay home that day of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I didn't stay very long; until early in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you get any sleep when you were at home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No. In the evening I went back to the Zvornik Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why did you go back to the Zvornik Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went back because I needed some rest. I had not had any sleep for the past two nights, and there was no one at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why didn't you get your rest at home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Because there was a possibility of someone coming to look for me, because of my work obligation. Because at the time, the security measures were at a very high level in all units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And there was a very large murder operation going on that security was involved with. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So about what time did you get back to the brigade headquarters on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: At about 7.00 in the evening, sometime in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: After I arrived, I went upstairs to the second floor where the sleeping quarters of the Zvornik Brigade headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went to my room and got some rest. I slept there that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Next morning, the morning of the 16th, about what time did you get up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly when, at what time, but I know that it was very early, at about 5.00 or 6.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I went down to the ground floor of the Zvornik Brigade command. I wanted to go to the restaurant to have something to eat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Tell us what significant events occurred that morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: As for the significant events that occurred on the 16th of July in the morning, it was the execution of Srebrenica Muslims who had been placed in Rocevic and Pilica. And the breakthrough of the remainder of Muslims who were going through Srebrenica to Tuzla in the area of Baljkovice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right And on the morning of the 16th, did you meet with anyone regarding what I will refer to as the murder operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic, chief security officer of the Zvornik Brigade; and Popovic, chief security officer of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And about what time was it that you saw Drago Nikolic and Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact hour. It could have been around 6.00, after 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this might be a good time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, can you tell us where you had this brief -- or this encounter with Mr. Popovic and Drago Nikolic in the early morning of 16 July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In the corridor on the ground floor of the Zvornik Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did either of them say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who said what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Popovic told me that I had to go to Rocevic or Pilica that day to get involved in the execution of Muslims who were detained there. Because of my previous experience in Orahovac, he said I was able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what else was said at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic was there as well, and he said that I couldn't go there because of my obligations here. And he said Pop, you go, Pop meaning Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In what context did this lieutenant say that to this lieutenant colonel, the chief of security of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The context being the fact that I had other obligations there, and that he should go instead. It was not an order, properly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How did Popovic respond to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He didn't say anything else to me. After this, I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was your duty that day of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That day of the 16th, I was the duty operations officer in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what time did that start?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: My shift started early in the morning, sometime earlier than usual, before 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And at any time that day did Popovic issue you any instructions to assist his operation to murder people up in the Pilica area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when did he issue you any instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the precise time. It was immediately after I took over my duties, so sometime after 7.00, between 7.00 and 8.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was he in person or was this over some communication that he issued you some instruction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He personally told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What instruction did he give you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He said that I should report to the Vlasenica command and the Bratunac command and see if they have a certain number of people to send to Rocevic and Pilica, because they were needed as assistants in the execution of Muslims who were detained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So what did you do when he gave you this instruction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: After I received this request, I made telephone contact with the Drina Corps command located at Vlasenica, that is with the Colonel -- Colonel Cerovic, to whom I had conveyed Popovic's request.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you remember what you actually said to Colonel Cerovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. I said to him that Popovic had been here and that he had told me to report to Vlasenica and Bratunac commands because he needed a number of people to be sent to the area of Rocevic and Pilica for the purposes of execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was this one of the open lines, or do you know if this was a secure line that you were speaking on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It was an open line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know if you spoke explicitly about executions or whether you tried to code it in some way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Not directly, not in this manner. Something to the effect that they should be sent over there, you know where, for the purposes of the operation to be carried out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did Cerovic respond to you when you passed on this request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He didn't say anything specific. He accepted it and he said that he would do it to the best of his capabilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, there was -- on the morning of the 16th, was there a need for troops to assist at the front line at Baljkovice about the same time that you make this request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you believe that Cerovic understood that you were talking about the murder operation and not the reinforcement for the combat operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Calls for speculation. The question can be rephrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can try something else, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, maybe you could try it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to believe that Mr. Cerovic misunderstood you in any way?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, objection. Calls for speculation. Now it's whether he misunderstood him. It presumes that he did, in fact, understand him that this was about the killing operation. I think it can be rephrased in a manner in which it's not suggestive to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But anyway, you ask this witness to testify about the other person's understanding of this message.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's not my particular meaning and I'll try to get it around another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Cerovic say anything to indicate he didn't understand what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. I don't think so this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if -- if he understood what he meant, I don't have a problem. In any event, I'll deal with it on cross, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe, Mr. McCloskey, you could ask the first part of the question. Just ask: Did Mr. Cerovic say anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Cerovic say anything after you passed on the request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He said that he would do what he could and that he would send as many men as he could and as many men as the circumstances were allowing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you mention that this request was from Popovic when you spoke to Cerovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did -- you said that Popovic requested you call another unit as well. Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who did you call?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who -- what other unit did you call?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I called Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know who you spoke to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I spoke to the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know that individual's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you -- how did you pass on the request from Popovic when speaking to the duty officer of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I told him that Popovic had been here to see me and that he wanted me to get in touch with Vlasenica and -- you -- with the request to send a number of men to join in the operation he was involved in. And also, that you should get in touch with Vlasenica, Colonel Cerovic, regarding the organisation of sending.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you get any -- what response, if any, did you get from the duty officer of the Bratunac Brigade at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I did not get any response.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, were they still on the line? What I mean is: Did he say anything to you after you told him this request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. Fine, we'll see what can be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And in your opinion, was there --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. It calls for speculation. He's asking for an opinion at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's nothing wrong with an opinion from this witness, not a darn thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if he's going to be asking about a state of mind, I even object to line of the question. I don't even want the question uttered. If he's going to be asking: In your opinion, was someone asking what you meant?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's not my question. Nice guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I think the opinion from this witness is allowed, and the question is how much weight we put on this piece of the evidence. Let the Prosecutor finish his question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In your opinion, was there any miscommunication on your part or any confusion on your part in communicating to the Bratunac Brigade duty officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back to a broader question, you were duty officer I think all the way even until the 17th of July. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you ever hear back from the Bratunac Brigade upon your request for reinforcements for Popovic and this operation related to Pilica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. How about, did you ever hear back from Vlasenica or Cerovic about Popovic's request that you had passed on to them for reinforcements, related to Popovic's murder operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Later on in the day were there some communications regarding reinforcements for the combat operation out at Baljkovice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We'll -- when we get to those exhibits, we can -- I'll ask you more particular questions. I want to show you now an exhibit. It should be marked -- 133 is the English version, 133/B is the B/C/S version. And I've got an original -- a colour copy of the original with the dates marked on it. If I could show this to the witness. And opening it to page -- well, to the date of July 16, page 26 in the English and last three digits, 763 in the -- yeah, 763 in the B/C/S. First of all, can you take a look at this copy and tell us what this book is a copy of, if you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: This is the logbook of the duty officer, duty operations officer of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And this particular logbook, what is its function and purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Jotting down notes in the course of the watch, messages, requests received, reports, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Is there another duty officer's logbook that is a more formal book that is written in a more formal way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. There is the book of reports sent to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We have been referring to this book as the duty officer workbook so -- just for clarity, I will be referring to this exhibit, 133, as the workbook you described as people put notes in or the duty officer puts notes in. And could you look at what is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could you look at what is marked as -- well, does this look like a genuine book or a copy of a genuine book?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If that's the original book -- excuse me, if this is the original book, then it shouldn't be a copy of the book. It either is the original or it is not the original. So which one is it. And it's not whether it looks like one but whether he recognises that document, and then the next question should be: What do you recognise it to be, and how do you so recognise it. In that line of questioning, I don't have a problem. But if that is the original one that was kept, then he should be able to identify it if the gentleman knows it, not if it's a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the Prosecutor is going to rephrase his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that -- I really don't want to rephrase my question, because it meant to -- this is not the real book, and that's what I'm asking him. Is this a copy of a real book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I can try that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this a copy of a real book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how do you know that this is a copy of a real book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: These are my notes that I took in the course of my watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Is this -- do these notes reflect the notes that you took on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me then go to what is in the B/C/S -- in your book, the last three numbers, which are the red numbers, 763. If you could go to that page. Do you see what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, I don't mean to interrupt here, but if this is a copy of the real book, then where is the real book so at least we can compare this to the real book. I think there's a problem with authentication. I understand that this may be something that the gentleman kept as a diary, as one of his private possessions. But if there is an original book, where is it so we can compare that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To my understanding, I believe this document has already been admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now this gentleman is saying this is his copy, unless I'm understanding the question, the way it's being phrased. So when was this copied? Was it copied contemporaneous at the time? Was it copied afterward so that they could have some safe keeping, you know so they could have something later on in the event that when they came here to the Tribunal, I don't know. But he's saying that this was a copy of the original one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, to me, there's no problem. But for the sake of the record, Mr. McCloskey, maybe you could lay some foundations on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And your recollection is correct. This book is in evidence, and I'm sure Mr. Karnavas just has forgotten all the foundation that went into this, because it was mostly for Zvornik. But this person doesn't really know much more than that's the handwriting in his book, as far as I know. And I can refer the Court and Mr. Karnavas to all the testimony of Dragan Obrenovic and how he got the original of the book and all that that was the foundation that provided it into evidence in the first place and that he recognised certain handwriting in it and the situation where he got it from and all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not that I don't recollect. It's the way the question was posed that this was his book, as if a personal book. Now with the qualification being made by Mr. McCloskey, I don't have a problem with the questions posed. He wrote in this book, but to say that it's his, meaning his and his alone, this witness's, I have a problem with that. And that's not my understanding, that that's what this book reflects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think there's a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't want to lead the impression that this is his book. This is the book used by the duty officer, as he's described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I couldn't see where it is, you know. But I imagine if it is his book. But you may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this is not the original book that you're looking at in front of you right now, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes -- no, no. That's not the original book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. Thank you. Have you had a chance to see the actual original book at some point in the last few months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. No, no, that's not the original book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, thanks. Thank you. Have you had a chance to see the actual, original book at some point in the last few months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you also had a chance to study this book and take it home, the copy that -- like the one you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And so you recognise your handwriting in this copy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to page -- last three digits 763 of those stamped red numbers that are on the top of the page. And there's a reference that starts 0855 Golic, it's page 26 of the English. Do you see that in your book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And I just want to ask you about a few of these entries. The one 0855, Golic asked Popovic to call him and said that he can forget what he asked for and what he wrote about. He knows what he is supposed to do according to the agreed procedure. "Boss from Panorama (01). Message conveyed to Popovic at 0910." Do you know anything more about this than what is said here, this cryptic message?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I know only that he sent in the request, as is stated here, and I know that the message was conveyed to him. He knew what he had agreed at Panorama 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When it says: "Boss from Panorama 01," what's Panorama 01?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Panorama was the code name for the Main Staff, and 01 refers to General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And so did you convey this message to Popovic at 9.10, like it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall how you conveyed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I conveyed it over the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know where Popovic was -- well, let me ask you: Who were you talking to -- who was on the other end of the phone when you conveyed this message to Popovic, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Popovic was at Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So where was the phone located that he was speaking on, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where the phone was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, do you remember where you called? Was it a public number? A private number? A military number? I mean, do you have any idea where it was that you were calling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It was a military number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And to what military unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The 1st Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is their headquarters near Pilica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Not near Pilica, but there was a phone located near Pilica. That was where a signalman was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And let's go to -- I think the bottom of the page there's an entry that says Beara to call Panorama 1.55 at 0930 hours." Is that your handwriting? Do you see that section? It should be on the bottom of page 763.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that your handwriting in this exhibit, 133?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And we know who Beara is, but do you know who is Panorama 155?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Panorama is the code name for the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what's 155?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't know what that refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Did you receive a call from Panorama?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is this little note you took a reflection of your receiving that call?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go to the next page, it's English 27; in yours it would be the last three digits 763. There is an entry that says: "At 1.15 hours, it was reported from Zlatar that triage of wounded and prisoners must be carried out, and it was reported to Beara." Did you -- is that in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Have you seen an intercept that talks about Beara and triage like this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, first here what does it mean, that: "It was reported to Zlatar that treatment of wounded and prisoners must be carried out." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That the execution of the prisoners and wounded should be carried out in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you report that message to Beara, as it says here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you do that in person or by some sort of communication means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the next one says: "At 11.20 hours, Badem, Colonel Jankovic was looking for Major Malinic." Is that in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is Badem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That is the code name for the unit from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what does this mean, that Colonel Jankovic was looking for Major Malinic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Colonel Jankovic wanted Major Malinic to report to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At that time did you know who Colonel Jankovic was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you know who Major Malinic was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you convey that message to anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. I conveyed it to the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could go to exhibit 250, an intercept of 16 July at 1111 hours. If you could take a look at the B/C/S version of that, and we can put the -- well, let's not. Let's just hang on to the English. Now, if you could just take a -- I won't read all of this, but if you could just take a look at it. Can you tell us who X is in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is this the conversation that in part is reflected in the book, Exhibit 133, that we just talked about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when X, or you, says: "Colonel Beara is right here by me," where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That was in the duty operations officer's room, the duty operations officer of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go back to the workbook, to your page 766; English 29. And the section I want you to take a look at, it says: "At 1400 hours, Popovic requested a bus with a fuel tank and 500 litres of D2. And Zlatar duty officer and Golic informed." Again, is that note in your writing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know what this had to do with, this fuel request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: For the operation of the execution in the Pilica area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I know that because I knew where Popovic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you know what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. I know where he was and I knew that he was carrying out the executions of Muslims who were located in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So did you -- what did you think the fuel was for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The fuel for the transportation and for the continuation of the operation of the killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The transportation of the Muslim prisoners, you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could briefly look at Exhibit 252, an intercept, 16 July, at 1358 hours. Again, take a look at the B/C/S. I know you've had a chance to see this before, so just take a brief look at it. It mentions the Palma duty officer. Who's that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's talk about 500 litres of D2 for Popovic and Pilica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that the same operation that you took a note on in the workbook that we just talked about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back to the workbook. And we'll skip up to page 34 in the English; page, last three digits, 771 in the B/C/S. And what I want to ask you about is this section that says: "At 2210 hours, the first battalion asked for one loader, one excavator, and a dump truck with a tarpaulin to be in Pilica at O800 hours." Is that in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At the time did you know what the loader and excavator and dump truck were needed for on 16 July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what was that, up at the 1st Battalion area? What was it needed for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: For the execution of the Muslims who were there, for the digging of the pits, and their burial.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And in that same section it says: "Conveyed to Jokic and Milosevic." Did you write that note: "Conveyed to Jokic and Milosevic"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so what does that note mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: That they were notified that the machinery has to be supplied and that it has to be sent to a certain area at a certain time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who notified them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who is this Jokic that you notified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Jokic was the chief of the engineer unit in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who is this Milosevic you notified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Captain Milosevic was the assistant to the commander for logistics in the Zvornik Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why would you need to notify the logistics commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: To include him to provide assistance regarding a truck, if the engineer unit did not have the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you conveyed this message to Mr. Jokic, do you recall anything that he may have said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know how you conveyed it to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Over the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know where he was when you phoned him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The command of the engineer unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In Kalesija area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was at the command of the engineering unit in Kalesija or whether he was at the command of the Zvornik Brigade when you spoke to him, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: At the command of the engineering unit of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that command was located where at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Approximately 2 kilometres from the Zvornik Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: North of the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: From the command, as you go in the direction of the Petkovci village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to English page 36; B/C/S 773. If you could go to 773 and take a look at the last line there on that page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Now, in this section it says: "The 1st Battalion asked if the engineer machines had been secured. Situation is normal. (redacted) to report." Do you recognise that handwriting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you know whose handwriting that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Whose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Of the assistant to the duty operations officer of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know that person's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I know that his name is Andjelko. I don't know his surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What part of the brigade was he from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He worked at the personnel section of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember his rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was he an officer, lieutenant or above?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No, he was not an officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know what this means: "(redacted) to report"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: To provide report whether this has been secured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go to an exhibit, another intercept, 257, 16 July, 2116 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to private session on this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want to register my unhappiness with respect to what just happened. Because here we're shielding from the public exactly that Mr. Blagojevic did not send anybody to do any killings. Just by coincidence, the two most important intercepts are covered in private session. And I must say, I am rather frustrated at this point, Your Honour. I know that you're making the right decisions, but I must register my frustration. And perhaps it's late in the evening and I'm a little testy, but I am a little frustrated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I already said that we will look into it. Any important piece of the evidence we'll take into consideration. There's no problem about that. You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, as you're aware, Mr. Butler cleared up this issue a long time ago. The Prosecutor is not contesting it. These comments are absurd and unnecessary by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, after the events of July 13th through 17th, did you become aware of an operation to rebury the Muslim victims that were buried in the mass graves around Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When did you first become aware of this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Two months later, approximately. I cannot remember exactly how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how did you become aware of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Drago told me that there was a possibility of mass graves being dislocated, the mass graves in the area of Zvornik, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then tell us what else you learned and when.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the first sentence the witness said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe one month after that, I heard from Popovic, the chief security officer of the Drina Corps, at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters in the office of the chief security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what did you hear? What was said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He said that the mass graves were going to be relocated, the mass graves in the area of Zvornik, and that I should get involved on behalf of the Zvornik Brigade command in order to assist the group which was supposed to carry out the work, also in order to issue fuel and to monitor the use of fuel that would be allocated to me and that would be sent on my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who was present at the security office when he told you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic, the Zvornik Brigade chief security officer was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And any other information he provided at -- on that date about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He told me that the Zvornik Brigade force engineers should also get involved in this operation, and that they should work together with the force engineers of the 5th Infantry Battalion of the Drina Corps, and that work should start immediately, that is, after all this has been arranged for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So what did you do to assist in this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: As soon as I received the tasking and as soon as the means to carry out the -- this operation arrived, I met with Mr. Jokic to see which particular group would be involved. And he said there should be no problems, that there was nothing to worry about, that a group had been assigned to do the job for the engineering unit. And he introduced me to the -- to a representative of this group who was to be involved in this work; he introduced me to the member -- a member of this engineering unit, Lazarevic -- I don't know what his name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And which Jokic is this that's introducing you to Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The chief of the engineering unit of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what else did you do related to this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I was introduced to Lazarevic, and I told him what the upcoming tasks would be. I told him also that he should get in touch with the representatives of the force engineers of the 5th Battalion in order to secure new pits where the existing ones should be relocated. And I asked him whether he knew all those locations, and how the work should be done. He said he did, because they had already visited those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How much before the actual digging started did you have this meeting with Mr. Jokic where he introduced you to Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: It could have been 15 or 20 days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what did you do in relation to the actual programme itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: The fuel that I received I then issued to Lazarevic, the fuel for the machines, the construction machines that were going to be used for the excavation. He was in daily contact with the other side, that is the engineering unit of the 5th Battalion. So as they were digging new pits, he was following up with the relocation of the primary graves. I also told him that an average of between 80 and 100 should remain in the primary graves, which was the request of Popovic, the security officer of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did Popovic tell you why he wanted 80 to 100 bodies to remain in the primary graves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He said that should an examination of those graves be carried out, should an inquiry be made into the reasons of the existence of those graves, this would then show that this was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to what the Zvornik Brigade engineers were actually doing in this operation, aside from you distributing fuel to Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. They were involved in the digging out of those mass graves, in the transport of those bodies to the new graves, which had been dug out by the members of the 5th Battalion, the engineering unit of the 5th Battalion, in other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How did you know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I knew this because Popovic had made an indication of that in a map. He had a diagram of the new graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, how did the diagram indicate who was doing what, if it did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: This was not indicated in the diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So how do you know the Zvornik Brigade was actually involved in digging, not just distributing fuel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I know because I was in contact with Lazarevic. And I had requested from Mr. Jokic to tell me what the work per hour of the construction machines would be, so that I can justify the expenses in terms of fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When did you have this contact with Mr. Jokic about the use per hour of the machines, in relation to when the digging operation was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes. After the completion of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you say anything to Mr. Jokic about what this fuel was -- what project you were involved with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what did you say to him about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I told him that the fuel had been sent to me for the construction machines that were going to be involved in the operation, and that I had to justify the expenses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did Jokic respond to you when you said this to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, he said what the consumption of those machines would be per hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what kind of machines was he talking about, were you and he talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: He was talking about excavators and loaders, and also about a truck which was used for transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with anyone from the 5th Engineering Battalion about this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes, one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What was that and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: This was just before the beginning of the operation of the relocation of existing graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what was communicated between you? First of all, who was this person from the 5th Engineers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: I don't know the name of the person, but I was told from the 5th Engineering Battalion that I had to give them 500.000 litres of fuel so that they could start the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Do you have any information that would indicate the command of the Zvornik Brigade was aware of this reburial operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: First, that Popovic, chief of security, and Drago, they had arrived from the room normally used by the commander and chief of security; this was the first piece of information that I got. And then the second one was that the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Vinko Pandurevic, was notified of the relocation operation, and that the people who participated in this work were eventually given three days off and three sacks of washing powder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, how do you know --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Two bags of 1 kilo each -- 3 kilos each.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How do you know that the people who were involved in this were given days off and washing powder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Pandurevic, the brigade commander, told me that he would say this to the commanders of the units who had taken part in the work, and he told this to Sretan Milosevic, the logistics officer. That is, he told him that this washing powder should be given to them so that they could wash the clothes that they had worn during the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So Mr. Pandurevic told this to you directly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And was Milosevic in the room as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And aside from the days off and the washing powder, how do you know that Pandurevic was informed of it, the murder -- the reburial operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Because after it was completed, I notified him of that fact. And Popovic and Drago Nikolic had come from there, from those rooms before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, you say that you notified Pandurevic of what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: After the completion of the operation for the relocation of the mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was this done personally or over some communication means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: Personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One last question. Your communication with Mr. Jokic regarding how much fuel was used with -- for the machines, was that done in person or over some communication means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-130
utterances.text: In person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. I don't have any further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think it's time for the break. We are about 2 minutes past the time. And tomorrow afternoon, we'll continue with the cross-examination. And, Witness, I'm afraid you have to stay here for another day, so you have to remember that you're still under oath during that period, so do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. I have one more exhibit, which we can do tomorrow. It will just take, hopefully, a minute. I just noticed I forgot it, but it will need to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think there's no problem to give him 1 minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Far be it from me to deny him that 1 minute he would need to wrap it up. He can have 2, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you for your generosity. Well, the hearing for today is adjourned. We'll resume tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 7.04 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 27th day of January, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.
